runs/runs: Train the same kind of model with more and more compute, C: the total arithmetic of training, counted in floating point operations, or FLOPs. Each dot is one run's final loss, L.
runs/flat: On ordinary axes the loss plunges, then flattens, and most of the runs crowd into one corner.
runs/log: Now space both axes by powers of ten, so that every step to the right is ten times the compute. These are log-log axes.
runs/line: The runs fall on a straight line. That is a scaling law.
why/law: The law says L equals a times C to the minus alpha. The numbers a and alpha, the Greek letter alpha, are fixed by fitting the runs. Alpha is the scaling exponent.
why/logs: Take logs to base ten, written log base ten, or here just log. They count powers of ten: the log of ten to the twenty is twenty.
why/power: Like ln, a log to base ten turns a product into a sum. So it turns a power into a multiple: ten cubed, squared, is ten cubed times ten cubed, so its log is three plus three, six: two times three.
why/minus: The same holds for the power minus alpha: the log of C to the minus alpha is minus alpha times the log of C. With C at ten to the twenty and alpha at zero point one, that is minus zero point one times twenty: minus two.
why/line: So log L is log a, minus alpha times log C: a straight line, with slope minus alpha.
why/slope: Read the slope off two runs. From ten to the eighteen to ten to the twenty FLOPs, two powers of ten, log L falls from zero point six to zero point four. Minus zero point two over two: a slope of minus zero point one.
tenfold/step: Each power of ten in compute moves log L down by alpha. In plain numbers, that multiplies the loss by ten to the minus alpha.
tenfold/ex: With alpha at zero point one, the factor is zero point seven nine. Ten times the compute takes a loss of three point one six down to two point five one.
tenfold/hundred: A hundred times the compute is two such steps: zero point seven nine times zero point seven nine. That is ten to the minus zero point one, twice, and multiplying adds the powers: ten to the minus zero point two, about zero point six three. The loss reaches about two point zero.
tenfold/k: So k factors of ten in compute multiply the loss by ten to the minus k alpha. A thousand times the compute is three factors: ten to the minus zero point three, about a half.
tenfold/cost: Each cut by that same fraction costs another ten times the compute, so every gain asks for a far bigger run than the last.
tenfold/back: Run it backwards, too. Say each tenfold step multiplies the loss by zero point eight. How much more compute takes a loss of four down to two point five six? Two point five six over four is zero point six four, which is zero point eight times zero point eight: two factors.
tenfold/factors: Each factor costs ten times the compute, so two of them cost ten times ten: a hundred times the compute.
